relevant_findings.topic: Vinyl siding has a single repaint substrate state
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike wood siding repaint which has 5 substrate states (sound, chalking, failing, peeling, weathered), vinyl siding repaint has ONE valid state: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT. Vinyl always has a factory-applied PVC finish — it is never bare, never stained, never clear-coated. The factory finish is integral to the material. Vinyl condition is binary: sound (repaintable) or physically damaged (replacement, not painting). There is no DSD gradient for vinyl — the PVC substrate does not degrade like wood fibers.

relevant_findings.topic: LRV class is the primary configuration variable replacing DSD
relevant_findings.finding: Where wood siding repaint's dominant cost driver is DSD (substrate deterioration), vinyl's dominant variable is LRV class. Standard colors (LRV 55+) follow the baseline material path. IR-reflective colors (LRV 35-55) require specialty pigment products that cost more but do not change labor time. LRV <35 is a HARD STOP — no override available. This makes lrv_class a true configuration dimension that drives material selection and gates color approval.

relevant_findings.topic: 100% acrylic latex binder is the only acceptable binder for vinyl
relevant_findings.finding: Alkyd, oil-based, and hybrid formulations are PROHIBITED on vinyl siding. PVC panels expand and contract thermally up to 5/8 inch per 12-ft panel. Only 100% acrylic latex has sufficient flexibility to accommodate this dimensional movement. Alkyd/oil coatings crack and delaminate within 12-24 months on vinyl. This is a hard material constraint — no override, no exception.

relevant_findings.topic: Adhesion primer is mandatory — STIX class solvent-attack bond
relevant_findings.finding: High-solids adhesion primers (Insl-X STIX, Benjamin Moore Fresh Start) are required for all vinyl siding repaints. These formulations 'bite' into the PVC surface through solvent attack, creating a chemical bond rather than relying on mechanical adhesion alone. Standard exterior primers do NOT adhere to vinyl's low surface energy. This is not state-dependent — adhesion primer is ALWAYS required regardless of vinyl condition.

relevant_findings.topic: Heat deflection temperature limits dark color application
relevant_findings.finding: Standard PVC siding has a heat deflection temperature of approximately 165 degrees F. Dark colors add 20-50 degrees F to surface temperature under direct sun. On a 95 degree F day with full sun, a dark-painted vinyl panel can exceed 165 degrees F and permanently warp or buckle. IR-reflective pigment technologies (VinylSafe, Colors for Vinyl) reflect near-infrared radiation, allowing colors down to approximately LRV 35-40 without exceeding thermal limits.

CertainTeed, Mastic, and Westlake Royal explicitly void coverage for unauthorized alterations or thermal distortion caused by dark paint. Painting vinyl siding voids the manufacturer's finish warranty in all cases. Contractor provides a 5-10 year workmanship warranty in lieu of manufacturer coverage. Client must acknowledge warranty void before work proceeds. A proper repaint extends siding service life by 7-15 years.

relevant_findings.topic: Vinyl can chalk from UV degradation
relevant_findings.finding: Although less severe than aluminum chalking, vinyl PVC surfaces can develop chalk from UV degradation of the surface layer. Chalk must be removed before priming — residual chalk acts as a bond-breaker between substrate and adhesion primer. Washing with alkaline cleaner in a downward spray pattern addresses chalk removal. This is a prep requirement, not a substrate state change (vinyl remains SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT with light chalk).

relevant_findings.topic: Spray is primary application method with brush detail for J-channels
relevant_findings.finding: Airless spray is the primary application method for vinyl siding field. Unlike wood siding, vinyl does NOT require backbrushing — the non-porous PVC surface does not absorb coating into fibers. Brush/roller detail work is needed only for J-channels, under-sill channels, and cut-in at trim transitions. Production rates: spray 400-500 SF/hr (higher than wood because no backbrush), brush detail 125-175 SF/hr.

relevant_findings.topic: No RRP/lead-safe gate required for vinyl siding
relevant_findings.finding: Vinyl siding is a post-1960s product that was never manufactured with lead-based coatings. The factory PVC finish is not a paint coating — it is integral to the material. Therefore, EPA Lead-Safe RRP requirements do not apply to vinyl siding repaint. This eliminates a major cost variable present in wood siding repaint specs.
relevant_findings.source: Researcher analysis; vinyl siding product history

relevant_findings.topic: No stain-blocking or tannin management needed
relevant_findings.finding: Vinyl (PVC) does not contain tannins, wood extractives, or any water-soluble bleeding agents. Unlike wood siding repaint where tannin-rich species require alkyd stain-blockers, vinyl has zero stain-bleed risk. The adhesion primer serves only an adhesion function, not a stain-blocking function.

When multiple coats are applied, labor distributes: 1st coat = 50% of total labor (full prep, first pass, learning the surface), 2nd coat = 30% (familiar surface, better coverage), 3rd coat = 20% (smooth surface, minimal touch-up). Standard vinyl repaint is primer + 1-2 finish coats depending on quality tier.

Multi-story vinyl siding work adds +50% labor to all tasks due to ladder setup, repositioning, and reduced production at height. This aligns with FAC_EXT_ACCESS ladder tier (1.35-1.50 modifier range). Access modifier applies uniformly to all task types (wash, mask, prime, paint, detail).

relevant_findings.topic: Pressure washing is mandatory first step
relevant_findings.finding: All vinyl siding repaint requires pressure washing as the first production step. Wash removes dirt, mildew, chalk residue, and surface contamination that would prevent adhesion primer bond. Downward spray pattern with alkaline cleaner (TSP or dedicated siding cleaner). Rate: 500-1000 SF/hr. Must dry completely before primer application (24-48 hours typical).

relevant_findings.topic: PCA P14 Level 2 is the baseline prep standard
relevant_findings.finding: PCA P14 governs surface preparation levels for exterior siding. Level 2 (Standard) is the baseline for exterior siding repaints — washing, scraping of loose material, and light sanding. For vinyl, this simplifies to washing and light scuff since there is no loose paint to scrape (factory finish is integral to PVC).

condition_drivers.impact: Single state — vinyl always has factory finish intact. No state-dependent branching for prep or primer. Adhesion primer is always required. Prep is always wash + light scuff. This dramatically simplifies the spec compared to wood siding repaint (5 states).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION with only one valid value. Vinyl condition is binary: sound (this spec applies) or physically damaged (replacement scope, not painting).

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy — wash, adhesion prime, single finish coat. Standard-grade 100% acrylic. QT3: standard — wash with TSP, adhesion prime, two finish coats, brush detail at J-channels and cut-in. Mid-grade 100% acrylic. No QT4/QT5 — vinyl is not a fine-finish substrate.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. QT3 adds a dedicated detail coat for J-channels, under-sill areas, and cut-in quality — this is the primary labor difference between tiers.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives color selection gate and material path. standard_55+ = any 100% acrylic exterior latex. ir_reflective_35-55 = IR-reflective pigment products only (VinylSafe, Colors for Vinyl type). LRV <35 = HARD STOP — not a configuration option, it is rejected. lrv_class does NOT change labor — it changes material selection and cost.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION unique to vinyl siding. Replaces DSD as the key decision variable. LRV <35 is an absolute gate — the estimation engine must reject any color selection below LRV 35.

condition_drivers.impact: Spray is primary method for vinyl siding field. No backbrushing required (unlike wood). Brush/roll for J-channels and detail only, or when spray is not feasible (wind, neighbor proximity). Method affects protection zone escalation (spray = more masking of adjacent surfaces).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Note: NO spray_backbrush option — vinyl does not absorb coating, so backbrushing serves no purpose.

condition_drivers.impact: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation. Unlike wood siding repaint, access modifier does NOT stack with DSD multiplier (no DSD dimension) — it is the only multiplicative modifier on production rates.
condition_drivers.notes: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition. Simpler cost impact than wood repaint because no DSD stacking.

quality_differences.description: Economy vinyl repaint. Pressure wash with detergent. Adhesion primer (STIX class), single coat spray. Single finish coat, 100% acrylic exterior. Minimal J-channel detail. No caulk replacement.
quality_differences.typical_use: Rental property, budget-constrained, pre-sale cosmetic refresh, color change on sound vinyl.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential vinyl repaint. Pressure wash with TSP or alkaline cleaner. Adhesion primer spray. Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior. Brush detail at J-channels, under-sill channels, and trim transitions. Caulk assessment at siding-to-trim joints. Clean transitions.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner repaint, color change, fade restoration. The most common tier for vinyl siding repaint.

failure_modes.name: Thermal warping from dark color application
failure_modes.description: LRV below 55 without IR-reflective pigments causes surface temperature to exceed PVC heat deflection threshold (165 degrees F). Vinyl panels permanently warp, buckle, or distort. Damage is irreversible — affected panels must be replaced. South and west exposures are highest risk.
failure_modes.prevention: LRV restriction: standard colors must be LRV 55+. Colors LRV 35-55 permitted ONLY with IR-reflective pigment products (VinylSafe, Colors for Vinyl). LRV <35 = absolute hard stop. Check LRV against sun exposure — full sun south/west facades are highest risk.
failure_modes.detection: Visible panel warping, buckling, or waviness. Gaps between panels. Panel edges lifting from J-channels. Develops within weeks to months of dark color application in warm season.

failure_modes.name: Delamination from alkyd/oil binder
failure_modes.description: Oil-based or alkyd coatings lack the flexibility to accommodate PVC thermal movement (up to 5/8 inch per 12-ft panel). Rigid coating cracks and delaminates from vinyl surface within 12-24 months. Complete coating failure — entire painted surface peels in sheets.
failure_modes.prevention: Lock binder to 100% acrylic latex ONLY. No alkyd, no oil, no hybrid formulations. Material specification must enforce this constraint. QC verification at material delivery.
failure_modes.detection: Coating cracking along panel length (perpendicular to expansion direction). Large sheets of paint peeling cleanly from vinyl surface. No substrate damage — vinyl surface is intact beneath failed coating.

failure_modes.name: Adhesion failure from skipping adhesion primer
failure_modes.description: Standard exterior primers do not bond to vinyl's low surface energy PVC material. Without a solvent-attack adhesion primer (STIX class), the finish coat sits on the surface without chemical bond. Entire coating system peels from vinyl in sheets, especially at panel expansion joints where thermal movement stresses the bond.
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory adhesion primer (STIX class). No exceptions, no shortcut. Primer must 'bite' into PVC via solvent attack for chemical bond. Standard latex primers, bonding primers designed for glossy latex, and all-purpose primers are NOT acceptable substitutes.
failure_modes.detection: Paint peeling in large sheets from vinyl. Clean separation — vinyl surface undamaged. Peeling concentrated at panel ends and expansion joints where movement stress is highest.

failure_modes.name: Painting over chalk residue
failure_modes.description: UV-degraded vinyl surface releases chalk powder. If adhesion primer is applied over chalk residue, primer bonds to chalk rather than sound PVC. New coating system fails at chalk layer — peels in patches rather than sheets.
failure_modes.prevention: Pressure wash with alkaline cleaner must remove all visible chalk. Hand-rub test after drying to verify removal. If chalk persists after washing, additional scrubbing or re-wash required. Do not prime until chalk is fully removed.
failure_modes.detection: Patchy peeling (not full sheets). White powder visible on back of peeled paint. Peeling concentrated on south/west facades where UV chalking was most severe.

failure_modes.name: Buckling from dark paint on south/west exposure
failure_modes.description: Even with IR-reflective pigments, dark colors on high-solar-exposure facades can approach thermal limits during extreme heat events. Panels may temporarily buckle during peak heat and return to normal at cooler temperatures (thermal cycling). Repeated cycling can cause permanent deformation.
failure_modes.prevention: For IR-reflective colors (LRV 35-55), consider facade orientation. South and west exposures face highest risk. Recommend lighter colors (LRV 55+) on high-exposure facades even when IR-reflective products are available. Document exposure risk in client warranty disclosure.
failure_modes.detection: Temporary panel waviness during hot afternoons. Progressive permanent deformation over multiple seasons. Most visible in long unbroken panel runs.

research_corrections.original_claim: Vinyl could arguably support QT2 only since it is purely functional (fade restoration, color change)
research_corrections.corrected_to: Keep QT2-QT3 range. QT3 adds a dedicated detail coat for J-channels, under-sill areas, and cut-in quality. QT3 also includes two finish coats for better DFT and durability, plus caulk assessment. This is a meaningful quality difference worth preserving.

research_corrections.original_claim: Multi-story modifier in doctrine is +50% labor which equals 1.5x
research_corrections.corrected_to: Confirmed alignment with FAC_EXT_ACCESS ladder tier. Doctrine +50% = 1.50x. Site_Condition_Vocabulary_Reference ladder = 1.35x, scaffold = 1.60x. The doctrine's +50% is a simplified approximation — use the canonical access_type modifiers from Site_Condition_Vocabulary_Reference for estimation (ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50). No correction needed — confirm alignment.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief, cross-referenced with Site_Condition_Vocabulary_Reference.md)

research_corrections.original_claim: Vinyl chalk is not a concern (only aluminum chalks severely)
research_corrections.corrected_to: Vinyl CAN chalk from UV degradation of PVC surface, though less severely than aluminum. Chalk residue acts as bond-breaker for adhesion primer. Washing must address chalk removal before priming. Added as prep requirement in RF-007. This does not change the substrate state (vinyl remains SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT) — chalk on vinyl is a surface contamination issue, not a coating failure mode like wood chalking.

key_decisions.decision: This spec covers ONLY vinyl (PVC) siding. Aluminum siding is excluded — it requires a separate spec (SF_SIDING_ALUMINUM_EXT_RP_v1).
key_decisions.rationale: Vinyl and aluminum have fundamentally different prep protocols (vinyl = adhesion primer via solvent attack; aluminum = self-etching primer + deoxidation), different failure modes (vinyl = thermal warping; aluminum = cohesive primer failure), and different material constraints. Combining them in one spec would create excessive branching complexity.

key_decisions.decision: Only one valid substrate state: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT. Vinyl is always factory-finished.
key_decisions.rationale: Vinyl siding has an integral PVC factory finish — it is never bare, stained, or clear-coated. Vinyl condition is binary: sound (repaintable under this spec) or physically damaged (replacement scope). There is no DSD gradient for vinyl — PVC does not degrade like wood fibers. Damaged panels are replaced, not painted.

key_decisions.decision: lrv_class is a configuration dimension with values: standard_55+ and ir_reflective_35-55. LRV <35 = hard stop.
key_decisions.rationale: LRV class drives color selection gate and material path. This is the dominant configuration variable for vinyl (replacing DSD from wood siding). It gates which products are eligible and whether the color can be applied at all. Material cost changes but labor does not.

key_decisions.decision: Quality tier range limited to QT2 and QT3.
key_decisions.rationale: Vinyl is not a fine-finish substrate. It has a uniform factory texture with no wood grain, no architectural detail, no handcrafted character. QT4/QT5 prep and inspection standards (raking light, filling surface defects, premium materials) provide no meaningful quality improvement on vinyl. The difference between QT2 and QT3 is coat count, J-channel detail, and caulk assessment — that is the full range of quality differentiation.

key_decisions.topic: No DSD dimension — vinyl condition is binary
key_decisions.decision: No substrate_condition (DSD) configuration dimension. No DSD prep multiplier.
key_decisions.rationale: PVC does not degrade progressively like wood. Vinyl does not rot, check, crack, or delaminate from moisture. It either has its factory finish intact (sound = repaintable) or is physically broken/warped (damaged = replace). There is no intermediate deterioration pathway to rate and price.

key_decisions.topic: Adhesion primer mandatory — no state-dependent selection
key_decisions.decision: STIX-class adhesion primer is ALWAYS required. No conditional logic.
key_decisions.rationale: Unlike wood siding repaint where primer type varies by substrate state (chalk-binding, stain-blocking, oil-alkyd penetrating), vinyl has one primer answer: high-solids adhesion primer that chemically bonds to PVC via solvent attack. No exceptions, no state branching.

key_decisions.decision: Finish coat binder locked to 100% acrylic latex. Alkyd, oil-based, and hybrid formulations are PROHIBITED.
key_decisions.rationale: PVC thermal expansion (up to 5/8 inch per 12-ft panel) requires flexible coating. Alkyd/oil crack and delaminate within 12-24 months. This is a hard material constraint enforced at specification level.

key_decisions.decision: Colors with LRV below 35 are rejected by the estimation engine. No override available.
key_decisions.rationale: Even with IR-reflective pigments, LRV <35 creates unacceptable thermal distortion risk. Vinyl heat deflection temp is 165 degrees F; dark colors can add 20-50 degrees F to surface temp. The risk of permanent warping is too high and damage is irreversible.

key_decisions.decision: Client must acknowledge manufacturer warranty void before work proceeds. Contractor provides 5-10 year workmanship warranty.
key_decisions.rationale: All major vinyl siding manufacturers (CertainTeed, Mastic, Westlake Royal) void warranty for unauthorized alterations. This is a client communication requirement, not an estimation item — but it must be documented in the scope workflow.

key_decisions.decision: Airless spray is primary method. NO backbrushing required (unlike wood siding). Brush detail only for J-channels and cut-in.
key_decisions.rationale: Vinyl is non-porous — coating does not absorb into fibers. Backbrushing serves no purpose on PVC. This increases spray production rate vs wood siding (400-500 SF/hr vs 150-250 SF/hr with backbrush).

key_decisions.decision: EPA Lead-Safe RRP is NOT applicable to vinyl siding repaint.
key_decisions.rationale: Vinyl siding is a post-1960s product. The factory PVC finish is integral to the material, not a lead-based paint coating. RRP requirements do not apply. This eliminates a major cost variable and simplifies the spec.

key_decisions.decision: When multiple coats are applied, labor distributes 50/30/20 per doctrine.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Vinyl_Aluminum_Siding_Doctrine.md Section 5. First coat = 50% of total labor (full prep, first pass). Second coat = 30% (familiar surface). Third coat = 20% (smooth surface). Standard system: primer + 1 finish (QT2) or primer + 2 finish (QT3).

notes_for_materials_manager: Primer: ALWAYS adhesion primer (STIX class) — Insl-X STIX SXA-110 or Benjamin Moore Fresh Start 023. These are the ONLY primers that chemically bond to PVC. Standard exterior primers, bonding primers for glossy latex, and all-purpose primers are NOT acceptable. Single coat spray application.

Finish coat binder: MUST be 100% acrylic latex exterior. Alkyd, oil-based, and hybrid formulations are PROHIBITED — they crack and delaminate within 12-24 months on vinyl. Verify binder type on PDS before approving any product.

LRV class drives material selection: standard_55+ = any approved 100% acrylic exterior (e.g., SW Duration Exterior, BM Regal Select Exterior). ir_reflective_35-55 = IR-reflective pigment products ONLY (e.g., SW VinylSafe colors, BM Colors for Vinyl). Must verify IR-reflective claim on PDS for any color LRV 35-55.
LRV <35 = HARD STOP. Do not source materials for any color below LRV 35 on vinyl siding. No exception, no override.

Coverage rates on vinyl: primer 300-400 SF/gal (smooth factory surface, single coat). Finish coat 350-450 SF/gal (smooth surface). Better coverage than wood siding repaint due to uniform factory texture.
No stain-blocking products needed — vinyl has no tannins or extractive bleeding. Adhesion primer serves adhesion function only.
Masking tape: blue tape (14-day) for trim transitions. Red stucco poly tape (30-day UV) for extended spray masking on high-adhesion surfaces.
Caulk for siding-to-trim joints (QT3 only): siliconized acrylic paintable caulk. Vinyl has low movement at joints — polyurethane not required.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup -> protect -> wash -> prep -> prime -> apply -> detail -> cleanup -> teardown. NOTE: No 'assess' module (unlike wood siding repaint) — vinyl condition does not require DSD rating, adhesion testing, or coating identification. Condition is binary: sound or damaged.

Wash module is MANDATORY first production step. Pressure wash with alkaline cleaner (TSP or siding cleaner) in downward spray pattern at 500-1000 PSI. Must remove all dirt, mildew, and chalk residue. Dry 24-48 hours before priming.

Prep module is MINIMAL: light scuff sand or liquid sander for adhesion tooth. No scraping (factory finish is integral PVC). No feather-sanding. No wood fiber treatment. This is dramatically simpler than wood siding repaint prep.
Prime module: adhesion primer (STIX class) spray application, single coat. Full coverage — no spot priming option (entire surface must receive adhesion primer for chemical bond to PVC).
Apply module: spray application, 100% acrylic latex exterior. QT2 = single finish coat. QT3 = two finish coats. NO backbrushing — vinyl is non-porous.
Detail module (QT3 only): brush detail at J-channels, under-sill channels, corner transitions, and trim cut-in. Rate: 125-175 SF/hr. This is the primary labor differentiator between QT2 and QT3.

WARRANTY VOID GATE: SOP must include warranty void acknowledgment step BEFORE any work begins. Client signs acknowledgment that painting voids manufacturer warranty. Contractor provides workmanship warranty terms.
LRV VERIFICATION GATE: SOP must include color LRV verification step. If color LRV is 35-55, verify IR-reflective product is specified. If LRV <35, STOP — do not proceed.
No RRP module — vinyl siding is never lead-painted.
No condition assessment module — vinyl condition is binary (sound = proceed, damaged = replace).
notes_for_estimation_engineer: This is a SIMPLER spec than wood siding repaint. No DSD prep multiplier, no substrate state branching, no RRP modifier, no condition assessment task, no scraping tasks, no stain-blocking. Primary cost variables: SF quantity x access modifier x coat count.

Production rates (QT3 baseline, ground access): pressure wash 500-1000 SF/hr, masking/prep 150-250 SF/hr, adhesion prime spray 350-450 SF/hr, finish coat spray 400-500 SF/hr, brush/roller detail 125-175 SF/hr.

Access modifier is the ONLY multiplicative labor modifier: ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. No DSD stacking (unlike wood siding repaint where DSD x access creates 2-3x compound multipliers).
Coat system: adhesion prime (1 coat always) + finish coats (QT2=1, QT3=2). Total coats: QT2=2 (prime+1 finish), QT3=3 (prime+2 finish).
Multi-coat time distribution (50-30-20): 1st coat (prime) = 50% labor, 2nd coat (1st finish) = 30%, 3rd coat (2nd finish) = 20%. Apply to spray coating tasks.

lrv_class does NOT change labor — it changes material cost only. standard_55+ and ir_reflective_35-55 have identical production rates. IR-reflective products cost more per gallon but apply at same rate.
Fixed-time tasks (per project, not area-scaled): warranty acknowledgment sign-off (0 labor — administrative), LRV verification (0 labor — administrative), equipment setup/teardown.
Board and batten vinyl: multiply flat SF by 1.10 for effective paintable area (less severe than wood board-and-batten 1.20x because vinyl profiles are less deep).
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation — SOP/process concerns only, not estimatable at bid time. Per established exterior spec convention.
J-channel detail labor: estimate at 5-10% of total field SF as detail SF, applied at brush detail rate (125-175 SF/hr). Only at QT3.
No caulk replacement at QT2. QT3 includes caulk assessment — estimate 50-100 LF of caulk at siding-to-trim joints per typical residential project.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Landscape protection from wash runoff and spray overspray. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base. Spray: full tarp over plantings + spray shield.
Mask windows during spray operations. Paper or masking film over glass. Only needed for spray method.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Mask trim elements when trim is different color from siding. Tape line at junction for brush/roll. Full paper mask for spray.
Mask exterior doors during spray operations. Full cover with masking film or plastic.
Cover AC units, heat pumps, and utility panels within spray zone. Full tarp coverage.
Protect soffit/fascia at eave junction if not being painted in same project. Tape line or paper border at siding-to-soffit transition.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Patios, walkways, and driveways within work zone. Drop cloth for brush/roll. Full tarp for spray.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during siding work is NOT this spec's responsibility when those surfaces have their own spec. If windows/doors are not being painted, their protection is scoped under this spec's masking zones. Protection responsibility follows surface ownership.
protection_zones_analysis.repaint_specific_note: Repaint on occupied homes has additional protection considerations: vehicles in driveways, outdoor furniture, pet areas. Client communication about work zone access is SOP, not estimation.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Corner trim at building corners. Often different (trim) color. Siding terminates at corner trim. Separate spec.
Window casing trim around openings. Siding terminates at casing. Separate spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Separate spec.
Fascia at roofline. Often white/light trim color. Separate spec.
Soffit underside at eave. Siding terminates at soffit/frieze junction. Separate spec.
Foundation below siding starter strip. Not painted in this scope.
Frieze board between siding and soffit. Trim color. Separate spec.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Siding field has NO edge work requirements. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs. Protection relationships only. Siding terminates at trim boards — no wet-edge blending across specs. Identical adjacency pattern as wood siding repaint.

affected_conditions.notes: Access type drives a HEIGHT MODIFIER on tasks. Applied per elevation. Simpler than wood siding repaint — no DSD stacking.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable at bid time and belong in SOP/process documentation, not production rate modifiers. Per established exterior spec convention.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Critical for spray but not estimatable.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, season. ESPECIALLY important for vinyl (165 degree F heat deflection) but not predictable at bid time. SOP concern.
Weather-dependent. Adhesion primer requires dry substrate but dew point is not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Important for vinyl thermal risk assessment but is scheduling/SOP, not estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: Vinyl siding has ONE valid input state. The factory PVC finish is always present and always 'sound paint' — it does not degrade like wood coatings. Vinyl condition is binary: sound (this spec applies) or damaged (panel replacement, not painting). No chalking state (vinyl chalk is surface contamination handled in wash step, not a substrate state), no failing/peeling state (vinyl finish does not peel — it is integral to PVC), no weathered state (PVC does not weather like wood fibers).

output_state.rationale: Output state is the new painted finish over vinyl. Satin or flat are common exterior sheens. Actual output varies by sheen selection.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Adjacent trim may be freshly painted (protect from siding spray overspray) or awaiting its own repaint (light mask sufficient).
Soffit at eave junction. If already repainted, light mask. If awaiting repaint, no protection needed.
Foundation wall is typically unpainted. Ground-level drop cloth handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Vinyl siding with factory PVC finish intact. Surface may have light UV chalking, dirt, or mildew — all addressed by washing. The factory finish provides the bond surface for adhesion primer.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Pressure wash with alkaline cleaner (500-1000 PSI, downward pattern). Dry 24-48 hours. Light scuff sand or liquid sander for adhesion tooth. No scraping — factory finish is integral to PVC.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Adhesion primer (STIX class) — always required, no exceptions. Solvent-attack chemical bond to PVC surface.
exterior_substrate_states.dsd_range: Not applicable — vinyl has no DSD gradient
exterior_substrate_states.pca_level: PCA P14 Level 2 (Standard) — wash and light surface preparation
exterior_substrate_states.notes: This is the ONLY valid state for vinyl siding repaint. Vinyl does not progress through deterioration stages like wood. If vinyl is physically damaged (cracked, warped, broken), panels are replaced — painting cannot address structural PVC damage.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks, not a site condition. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

scenarios.notes: Two-story siding, gable ends. Constant repositioning.
Large continuous areas above 8 ft. Less common for vinyl repaint vs wood (vinyl has less heavy prep work at height).
3+ story or difficult access. Rental cost.

exterior_access_type_analysis.vinyl_note: Access modifier impact is LESS severe on vinyl repaint vs wood repaint because there is no DSD multiplier stacking. On wood siding, DSD-2 on scaffold = 1.5x * 1.6x = 2.4x effective multiplier. On vinyl, scaffold = 1.6x only. This makes multi-story vinyl repaint proportionally less expensive than multi-story wood siding repaint.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints are documented here for SOP reference but are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per established exterior spec convention.

sop_reference_only.vinyl_note: Spray is primary method — wind is critical for vinyl siding work.

sop_reference_only.note: CRITICAL for vinyl: above 85 degrees F on vinyl risks flash drying and poor adhesion of STIX primer. Below 50 degrees F: slow cure of adhesion primer. Narrower range than wood siding.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Adhesion primer requires absolutely dry substrate for solvent-attack bond to PVC.

sop_reference_only.rule: Avoid application on sun-heated vinyl — especially dark IR-reflective colors. Apply on shaded side of building, work early morning on south/west facades.
sop_reference_only.note: Vinyl-specific concern: hot PVC surface affects primer bond quality.

pressure_wash.notes: Downward spray pattern, alkaline cleaner. Higher end for simple profiles, lower for areas with heavy soiling or mildew.

masking_prep.notes: Windows, trim, landscaping, hardscape. Rate includes tape, paper, plastic sheeting. Higher end for simple facades, lower for many openings.

adhesion_prime_spray.notes: STIX-class adhesion primer, single coat, airless spray. Full coverage required.

finish_coat_spray.notes: 100% acrylic latex, per coat. Higher rate than wood siding (no backbrush needed).

brush_roller_detail.notes: Cut-in, J-channels, under-sill channels, touch-up. QT3 only.

caulk_assess_replace.notes: Assess existing caulk + replace failed sections at siding-to-trim joints. QT3 only.

adjacency_notes: Vinyl siding field terminates at trim elements (corners, window casing, door casing, frieze) — no wet-edge blending across specs.
All adjacent surfaces are separate specs. Protection is the only cross-spec relationship.
Window/door protection during siding spray is managed by this spec's protection zones when those surfaces do not have their own active spec.
Foundation wall below siding starter strip is not painted — ground-level protection handled by landscape/hardscape zones.

assumptions.value: Repaint of existing vinyl (PVC) siding — factory finish intact. Exterior wall field surfaces only.
assumptions.note: Vinyl only — aluminum excluded to separate spec. Trim, windows, doors, soffit are separate specs.

assumptions.value: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT is the only valid state. Vinyl always has factory finish.
assumptions.note: Physically damaged vinyl = panel replacement scope, not painting scope.

assumptions.value: QT2-QT3 only. Vinyl is not a fine-finish substrate.
assumptions.note: QT4/QT5 standards provide no meaningful quality improvement on uniform PVC texture.

assumptions.value: LRV <35 is an absolute rejection gate with no override.
assumptions.note: Thermal distortion risk is irreversible. No contractor should accept this risk.

assumptions.value: EPA Lead-Safe RRP does not apply to vinyl siding.
assumptions.source: Product history — vinyl siding is post-1960s, never lead-painted
assumptions.note: Factory PVC finish is integral to material, not a paint coating.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine uses LRV 35 as the lower limit for IR-reflective products, but manufacturer-specific thresholds may vary by product line. Some IR-reflective lines may go slightly below LRV 35 while others may require LRV 40+.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use LRV 35 as the hard stop. Defer to specific product PDS for products claiming IR-reflective capability in the 35-40 range.

uncertainties.topic: Adhesion primer coverage rate on aged vinyl
uncertainties.detail: Doctrine rate of 350-450 SF/hr and 300-400 SF/gal is based on standard vinyl surfaces. Heavily chalked or UV-degraded vinyl may absorb more primer (STIX is a penetrating product), reducing coverage per gallon.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use lower end of range (300 SF/gal) for vinyl showing visible chalk after washing. Standard rate for clean vinyl.

uncertainties.detail: Wood board-and-batten uses 1.20x multiplier. Vinyl board-and-batten profiles are typically less deep than wood equivalents, so a lower multiplier (1.10x) is estimated but not field-calibrated.
uncertainties.recommendation: Field calibration with timed spray on vinyl board-and-batten vs flat lap profiles.

uncertainties.detail: Estimated at 5-10% of field SF for QT3 detail work, but actual J-channel complexity varies with window/door count and siding termination points.
uncertainties.recommendation: Derive J-channel detail SF from window/door count + perimeter edge count rather than percentage of field SF.
